Researchers in Switzerland, for example at the Agroscope bee research centre in Bern, are looking for new solutions against the mite.

begriffe.erklaerung: A very small arachnid with eight legs.
A living thing that lives on or in another and harms it.
A honeycomb cell in which a bee larva grows up.
A person who keeps bees and collects honey.

gewusst: Without treatment by beekeepers, there are hardly any wild honey bee colonies left in Europe.
Transferred to a bee, a varroa mite would be as big as a plate on a person.
The mite prefers drone brood, because it stays capped for longer.

teile.einleitung: Cold-blooded animals cannot hold their body temperature at a fixed value by themselves. Their body becomes as warm or as cold as their surroundings, so they are nimble when it is warm and sluggish when it is cold.
wichtigste: In cold-blooded animals the body temperature depends on the surroundings.
Fish, amphibians, reptiles, insects and most other animals are cold-blooded.
Birds and mammals, on the other hand, are warm-blooded.
In whitefish and perch the body temperature adapts to the water.
If a grass snake gets too cold, it becomes motionless.
Many cold-blooded animals warm up in the sun.
Cold-blooded animals need much less food than warm-blooded ones.

abschnitte.text: Cold-blooded animals produce only a little heat of their own. Their body temperature rises when it is warm and falls when it gets cold. The technical word for this is **poikilothermic**. The opposite are **warm-blooded** animals such as people, dogs and birds, which always stay at about the same warmth.

Fish such as catfish, perch and whitefish have about the temperature of the water they swim in. Reptiles such as the **sand lizard**, the slow worm and the grass snake are cold-blooded as well. Amphibians such as frogs and newts also belong here. Insects such as the cockchafer are cold-blooded too.

Cold-blooded animals control their temperature through their **behaviour**. A sand lizard lies on a warm stone in the morning to get going. If it gets too hot, it creeps into the shade. In summer, fish look for cooler, deeper layers of water.

When the temperature falls sharply, cold-blooded animals become slow and finally motionless. This state is called **cold torpor**. In winter, lizards, snakes and frogs creep into frost-proof places and stay there in winter torpor. Only when it gets warmer in spring do they wake up again.

Because they need no energy for heating, cold-blooded animals get by with little **food**. A snake can live for weeks without food after a big meal. A disadvantage is that in the cold they can hardly flee or hunt. That is why only a few reptiles live in cold regions, while in the tropics there are very many.

begriffe.erklaerung: The body temperature depends on the surroundings.
The body temperature always stays about the same, as in birds and mammals.
A state in which a cold-blooded animal becomes motionless because of the cold.
The technical word for cold-blooded.

gewusst: Bumblebees can warm up their flight muscles by shivering and so fly even in cool weather.
A person needs a large part of the energy in their food just to keep their body warm.
Some fish such as the great white shark can keep certain parts of the body warmer than the surrounding water.

teile.einleitung: Father Christmas is a figure from legend with a red coat and a white beard who brings presents at Christmas in many countries. According to the legend, he flies through the night in a sleigh pulled by reindeer.
wichtigste: Father Christmas is a figure from custom and legend.
His model is Saint Nicholas of Myra, a bishop from the 4th century.
In the legend, reindeer pull Father Christmas's sleigh.
The best-known reindeer is Rudolph with the red nose.
Reindeer really exist, and they live in the far north.
In Switzerland, the Christkind traditionally brings the presents, and on 6 December the Samichlaus comes.

abschnitte.text: Father Christmas is a friendly old man with a white beard, a red coat and a pointed hat. He is said to hand out presents to children on Christmas Eve. His model is Saint **Nicholas of Myra**, who was known for his generosity. In English-speaking countries he is called **Santa Claus**, a name that comes from the Dutch Sinterklaas.

Dutch emigrants brought the custom of Saint Nicholas to America. In 1823 a well-known poem appeared there in which Saint Nicholas flies through the air with a sleigh and eight **reindeer**. Illustrators and later advertisements made the picture of the plump man in the red coat famous all over the world. The reindeer **Rudolph** with the glowing nose was added only in 1939, through a story in the USA.

Reindeer live in the **tundra** and the northern forests of Scandinavia, Russia, Alaska and Canada. They are the only deer in which the females also carry antlers. Their broad hooves carry them well over snow and bog. In winter they scrape the snow away and eat mainly **reindeer lichen**.

In Lapland, the Sami have kept reindeer as domestic animals for centuries. Reindeer supply meat, hides and milk, and in the past they were also harnessed to sleighs. So it is not so far-fetched that in the legend reindeer pull the sleigh. Real reindeer cannot fly, of course.

In Switzerland, on 6 December the **Samichlaus** comes with his companion Schmutzli and often a donkey. He brings nuts, mandarins, gingerbread and chocolate. The Christmas presents on 24 December are brought, in many regions, by the **Christkind**. Through films and advertising, however, Father Christmas has become very well known here too.

begriffe.erklaerung: A kind of deer from the far north in which males and females carry antlers.
A cold, treeless landscape in the far north with mosses, lichens and dwarf shrubs.
Indigenous people in the north of Scandinavia and Russia, many of whom keep reindeer.
The Swiss name for Saint Nicholas, who visits children on 6 December.

gewusst: Reindeer can see light that is invisible to people, namely UV light.
When reindeer walk, their feet make a clicking sound.
In Finland, on the Arctic Circle, there is a village that is marketed as the home of Father Christmas.

teile.einleitung: The goat is one of the oldest domestic animals of humans. It is curious, clever and fond of climbing, and supplies milk, cheese, meat and wool. In Switzerland there are many breeds of goat of its own, which are kept mainly in the mountains.
wichtigste: The young of a goat is called a kid, the female a nanny goat and the male a billy goat.
Goats live in herds that are often led by an experienced lead nanny goat.
A nanny goat carries her kid for about 5 months in the belly.
Goats are ruminants and also like to eat thorny bushes.
Goats do not really eat old tins and paper, they only sniff at them.
Goats are clever and learn quickly how to get at food.
The domestic goat was tamed about 10,000 years ago in the Near East.

abschnitte.text: Goats have short to long fur that, depending on the breed, can be white, brown, black or spotted. Many goats carry horns and a beard on the chin. Their **pupils** are horizontal slits, so they take in a wide area and spot dangers early. With their hard, cloven hooves they climb safely over rocks.

Goats are **ruminants** with a stomach in four sections. They eat grasses, herbs, leaves, twigs and also thorny bushes that other animals avoid. In this way they help to keep **landscapes** open and to protect alpine pastures from becoming overgrown with scrub. That goats eat tins or paper is a myth, and they only curiously investigate such things with mouth and nose.

Goats are sociable animals and live in a **herd**. An experienced **lead nanny goat** leads the group, and the others follow her. Who is in charge is often settled with butting of heads. The goatherd looks after a herd.

After a pregnancy of about five months, the nanny goat usually gives birth to one or two **kids**. After a short time, often within minutes or hours, the little ones can stand and drink. A kid calls for its mother with loud bleating, and the nanny goat recognises it by voice and smell. Young goats like to play, jump about and climb on everything.

In Switzerland, around 80,000 goats live (in about 2023). Well-known Swiss breeds are the **Saanen goat**, the Toggenburg goat, the Chamois Coloured goat and the Valais Blackneck goat. The white Saanen goat from the Bernese Oberland is today one of the most important dairy goats in the world. In summer, many goats graze on the alps.

Researchers have shown that goats remember well how to get at food. In one experiment they learned to open a small food box, and still knew how months later. Goats can also tell apart the faces and voices of others of their kind. Their curiosity and urge to climb sometimes even lead them onto trees, roofs or steep rocks.

begriffe.erklaerung: The young of a goat.
A female goat.
An animal that brings its food back up and chews it a second time.
An experienced goat that leads the herd.

gewusst: In Morocco, goats climb argan trees to get at the fruit.
In Italy, ibex, the wild relatives of the goat, even climb steep dam walls to lick salt.
Goats are among the first animals that humans kept as domestic animals.

teile.einleitung: Alzheimer’s disease is an illness of the brain in which nerve cells gradually die. People with it become forgetful and, over time, need more and more help. It is the most common form of dementia.
wichtigste: The disease is named after the German doctor Alois Alzheimer.
He described it in 1906 in his patient Auguste Deter.
According to the WHO, Alzheimer’s makes up about 60 to 70 per cent of all cases of dementia.
Typical signs are beta-amyloid plaques outside the nerve cells and tau tangles inside them.
Usually the first difficulty is remembering new things.
The disease occurs mainly in older age.
It cannot be cured so far, but medicines can ease the symptoms.

abschnitte.text: The doctor **Alois Alzheimer** looked after the patient **Auguste Deter** in Frankfurt. She became more and more forgetful and confused. After her death, Alzheimer examined her brain under the microscope and found striking changes. In 1906 he presented his findings at a meeting of doctors in Tübingen. Later the disease was named after him.

In Alzheimer’s, lumps of protein build up between the nerve cells, the **beta-amyloid plaques**. Inside the nerve cells, the **tau protein** forms clumped bundles of fibres. As a result the cells can no longer work properly and die. One of the first regions affected is the **entorhinal cortex**, which is closely linked to memory. Over time the brain shrinks noticeably.

Usually the disease begins with difficulty remembering **new information**. People with it forget appointments or ask the same question several times. Old memories often last longer. Later it becomes hard to find your way around, find words or do everyday things. In the late stage, people depend on constant care.

The most important risk factor is **age**. Genes also play a part: the gene variant **ApoE4** is regarded as the strongest genetic risk factor for the late-onset form. But someone who has this variant will not definitely become ill. Exercise, mental activity and a healthy lifestyle can probably lower the risk a little.

Alzheimer’s still cannot be cured. Medicines such as **acetylcholinesterase inhibitors** can ease the symptoms for a while. They make an important messenger substance in the brain work for longer. Support in everyday life from relatives and carers is very important. In Switzerland, the organisation **Alzheimer Switzerland** advises people with the disease and their families.

gewusst: Auguste Deter was only about 50 years old when her forgetfulness began.
People with Alzheimer’s often still recognise music from their youth when they have forgotten much else.

teile.einleitung: The anvil is one of the three tiny bones in the middle ear. It lies between the hammer and the stirrup and passes sound on from the eardrum to the inner ear. Its Latin name is incus.
wichtigste: The anvil is called incus in Latin.
It is named after the blacksmith’s anvil.
It lies in the middle ear between the hammer and the stirrup.
It has two joints: one to the hammer and one to the stirrup.
Its long process is connected to the stirrup.
Unlike the hammer and the stirrup, no muscle is attached to the anvil.

abschnitte.titel: Where it is in the ear
abschnitte.text: The ear is made up of the outer ear, the middle ear and the inner ear. In the **middle ear**, a small air-filled cavity behind the eardrum, lie the three **ossicles**: the hammer, the anvil and the stirrup. The anvil sits in the middle. Together the three little bones form a chain that passes on vibrations.

The name comes from the **blacksmith’s anvil**, on which metal is worked. The Latin name **incus** also means anvil. The bone has a body and two processes, a short one and a long one. In anatomy books its shape is often compared with a **tooth** that has two roots.

The anvil is connected to its neighbours by **two joints**. With its body it sits on the head of the **hammer**. At the end of the **long process** it is connected to the **stirrup**. A tiny muscle is attached to the hammer and another to the stirrup. To the anvil, however, **no muscle** is attached.

Sound makes the **eardrum** vibrate. The hammer is fixed to the eardrum and passes the movement on to the anvil. The anvil transmits it to the stirrup, which presses against the oval window of the inner ear. In this way the sound is amplified and reaches the cochlea. If the connection between the anvil and the stirrup is broken, for example after an accident, you hear much worse in that ear. Often this can be put right with an operation.

gewusst: Even in newborn babies the ossicles are about as big as in adults.
The hammer, anvil and stirrup are the smallest bones in the human body.

teile.einleitung: The peregrine falcon is a powerful bird of prey and the fastest animal in the world. In a dive it swoops down on other birds at over 300 kilometres an hour. After it had almost disappeared in the middle of the 20th century, it has recovered well in Switzerland.
wichtigste: The peregrine falcon belongs to the falcon family.
It eats mainly other birds, which it catches in flight.
In its stooping hunt it plunges from a great height towards its prey.
In a dive it can reach speeds of over 300 kilometres an hour.
Adult peregrines have a blue-grey back.
Because of the poison DDT, it was badly threatened in the middle of the 20th century.
Pairs often stay faithful to the same partner for a long time.

abschnitte.text: The peregrine falcon is about as big as a crow, and the female is clearly bigger and heavier than the male. Adult birds have a **blue-grey** back and a light, cross-barred underside. Typical is the black **moustache stripe** under the eye, like a dark moustache. The wings are long and pointed, ideal for fast flight.

The peregrine falcon lives on all continents except Antarctica and is one of the most widespread birds in the world. It nests on rock faces, in quarries and, more and more often, on tall buildings in towns. Its scientific name is Falco **peregrinus**. The word comes from Latin and means wandering or foreign, because many northern peregrines migrate far south in winter.

The peregrine falcon eats mainly other birds such as pigeons, starlings and thrushes. In its **stooping hunt** it climbs high, folds its wings and plunges in a dive towards its prey. In doing so it can reach over 300 kilometres an hour. It strikes the prey in flight with its claws and afterwards usually carries it in its claws to a plucking place.

Peregrine pairs often stay faithful to the same partner for a long time and use the same nesting place for years. They do not build a nest of their own, but lay the eggs in a hollow on a rock ledge, the **eyrie**. The female usually lays three to four eggs, which are sat on for about a month. A wild peregrine falcon can live to be about 15 to 17 years old.

In the middle of the 20th century the pesticide **DDT** was used a great deal. It got into the bodies of birds of prey through insects and prey birds. As a result, the eggshells became so thin that they broke while being sat on. In many countries of Europe and North America the peregrine falcon almost completely disappeared, and in Switzerland too peregrines and other birds of prey suffered badly.

After DDT was banned in the 1970s, the populations slowly recovered. Protecting the nesting places from climbers and nest robbers also helped. Today the population in Switzerland has recovered clearly compared with the past. In some towns peregrines nest in nest boxes on church towers or tall buildings.

begriffe.erklaerung: A bird with sharp claws and a hooked beak that hunts other animals.
A hunt in which the falcon dives down on its prey from a height.
The nesting place of a bird of prey.
An insect poison used in the past that builds up in animals and is banned today.

gewusst: In a dive the peregrine falcon is faster than a Formula 1 car on the straight.
Peregrine falcons have been trained for hunting in falconry for centuries.

teile.einleitung: The eagle owl is a mighty owl with bright orange eyes and striking ear tufts. It is often regarded as the largest species of owl in the world and is a night hunter with very fine hearing. In Switzerland it nests mainly on rock faces in the Alps, in the Jura and in Ticino.
wichtigste: The eagle owl is often called the largest species of owl in the world.
Its eyes are typically orange.
Its hearing is much more sensitive than ours and helps it to locate prey in the dark.
With its very strong claws it grips and kills its prey.
The female usually lays 2 to 3 eggs and sits on them mainly alone.
Young eagle owls leave the nest before they can fly and clamber about as branchers.
Eagle owls react very sensitively to disturbance at the nesting site.

abschnitte.text: The eagle owl grows to about 60 to 75 centimetres tall and has a wingspan of up to 1.7 metres. The females are clearly bigger and heavier than the males and weigh up to about 3 kilograms. Its plumage is brown and yellowish with dark streaks, which makes it well **camouflaged**. Striking are the long **ear tufts** and the big orange eyes. It is often called the largest owl in the world, and only the Blakiston's fish owl in East Asia is similar in size.

Eagle owls live in Europe, Asia and North Africa. They need quiet nesting places, mostly on **rock faces**, in quarries or on steep slopes, and open country to hunt in. In Switzerland an estimated few hundred pairs nest, mainly in the Alps, in the Jura and in Ticino. Eagle owls stay in their territory all year round.

The eagle owl hunts at dusk and at night. With its very sensitive **hearing** and good eyes it finds prey even in the dark, and thanks to soft feathers it flies almost silently. It eats mice, rats, hedgehogs, hares and birds such as crows and pigeons. A strong eagle owl can occasionally even overpower young foxes or other birds of prey. Indigestible remains such as hair and bones it coughs up again as **pellets**.

How many eggs a female lays depends on the **food supply**, and it is mostly 2 to 3. The female sits on the eggs mainly alone for about five weeks. The male supplies her with food during this time. The young leave the nest before they can really fly and clamber about in the surroundings as **branchers**. If the parents are disturbed at the nesting site, they may even abandon the brood.

In the past the eagle owl was heavily persecuted and had almost disappeared in many areas. Today it is protected in Switzerland, but is still on the **Red List** of threatened breeding birds. Many eagle owls die on power lines, in road traffic or on fences. Climbers and photographers should avoid nesting cliffs during the breeding season. Wild eagle owls can live to be about 20 years old.

The German name Uhu comes from its deep call “buho”, which can be heard far away in late winter. With the call the male marks his **territory** and attracts a female. Often male and female call in a duet. In many legends and fairy tales the owl is a symbol of wisdom.

begriffe.erklaerung: Tufts of feathers on the head that look like ears but have nothing to do with hearing.
A ball of indigestible hair and bones that owls cough up.
A young owl that has left the nest but cannot really fly yet.
An area that an animal claims for itself and defends.

gewusst: An eagle owl can turn its head by up to 270 degrees.
The ear openings of the eagle owl lie hidden under the plumage at the edge of the face and not in the ear tufts.
In the eagle owl the female is bigger than the male, as in many birds of prey.

teile.einleitung: An actinic keratosis is a rough, scaly patch on the skin that arises from years of sun exposure. It is regarded as an early form of light skin cancer. It can be treated well, and good sun protection prevents it.
wichtigste: It is regarded as an early form of squamous cell carcinoma.
Typically it feels rough like sandpaper.
It often occurs on a bald head, the forehead and the backs of the hands.
The main trigger is chronic UV exposure over many years.
Single patches are often frozen with liquid nitrogen.
Field cancerisation means that the whole sun-damaged area is changed.
People who work a lot outdoors have a high risk.

abschnitte.text: The word “actinic” means “caused by rays”, meaning sunlight. A **keratosis** is a thickening of the horny layer of the skin. An actinic keratosis often looks like a small reddish or skin-coloured patch with scales. Typically it feels **rough like sandpaper**, and sometimes you feel it better than you see it. In dermatology it is regarded as an **early form of squamous cell carcinoma**, a form of light skin cancer. Not every patch turns into cancer, but the risk exists.

The main trigger is **chronic UV exposure over many years**. The skin does not forget: every sunburn and every long time in the sun harms the cells a little. That is why actinic keratoses occur mainly in older people, especially in places that are often exposed to the sun: **bald head, forehead, nose, ears and backs of the hands**. **People who work a lot outdoors**, for example in farming or on building sites, have an especially high risk. Fair skin is also more sensitive.

Often there is not just a single patch. Experts then speak of **field cancerisation**. This means that **the whole sun-damaged area of skin is changed**, even where you cannot yet see anything. That is why in such cases you treat not only the visible patches, but the whole affected area.

Single patches are often **frozen with liquid nitrogen**. The cold destroys the changed cells, and the skin then heals anew. For larger areas there are creams and **photodynamic therapy**: a substance that is applied makes the **diseased cells sensitive to light**, then the skin is illuminated, and the **light destroys** these cells. A dermatologist decides what suits best.

The best prevention is **sun protection** from an early age: a hat or cap, clothing, sunglasses and sun cream. You should avoid strong sun around midday. In the mountains the UV radiation is higher than in the lowlands, which matters in Switzerland when hiking and skiing. People who work outdoors should protect themselves especially well at work.

gewusst: UV radiation increases with every metre of altitude, and on a high mountain it is clearly stronger than by the lake.
Even on cloudy days a large part of the UV radiation reaches the skin.

teile.einleitung: Vertebrates are animals with an inner bony skeleton and a backbone. They include fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals, so also us humans. Although they make up only a small part of all animal species, many of the biggest and best-known animals are vertebrates.
wichtigste: All vertebrates have a backbone.
They have an inner skeleton of bone or cartilage and a skull that protects the brain.
They are usually divided into fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals.
There are about 70,000 known species of vertebrates.
More than half of all vertebrate species are fish.
Most animal species on Earth, however, are invertebrates such as insects.
The first vertebrates lived more than 500 million years ago in the sea.

abschnitte.text: The most important feature is the **backbone**, which supports the body and protects the spinal cord. Added to this is an inner skeleton that grows along with the animal. A **skull** surrounds the brain, and the most important sense organs such as eyes and ears sit on the head. Most vertebrates have two pairs of limbs, that is, fins, legs or wings.

**Fish** live in the water and breathe with gills. **Amphibians** such as frogs and newts usually begin their life in the water and later also live on land. Reptiles such as lizards, snakes and turtles have a skin with scales. Birds wear feathers, and mammals suckle their young with milk.

Fish, amphibians and reptiles are **cold-blooded**, and their body temperature depends on the surroundings. That is why lizards sunbathe in the morning. Birds and mammals are **warm-blooded** and keep their body temperature constant themselves. For this they need much more food than cold-blooded animals of the same size.

The first vertebrates arose over 500 million years ago and were small, jawless fish. Later, fish with jaws developed. About 370 million years ago the first vertebrates went onto land, and from them arose the amphibians. From these developed reptiles, and from their relatives came the **dinosaurs**, the birds and the mammals.

The biggest vertebrate, and at the same time the biggest animal of all time, is the **blue whale**, at over 30 metres long. Among the smallest vertebrates are tiny frogs from New Guinea that are smaller than a centimetre. Vertebrates live almost everywhere, in the deep sea, in deserts, in the high mountains and in the air. In Switzerland there live, for example, ibex, lammergeiers, fire salamanders and trout.

Animals without a backbone are called **invertebrates**. They include insects, spiders, worms, snails, jellyfish and many more. They make up about 95 per cent of all known animal species. Many of them have a hard shell on the outside instead of an inner skeleton.

begriffe.erklaerung: A chain of bones in the back that supports the body.
The bony framework of a body.
The body temperature depends on the surroundings.
The body itself keeps its temperature always about the same.
Animals without a backbone, for example insects.

gewusst: A human is more closely related to a trout than the trout is to a squid, because humans and trout are both vertebrates.
Sharks have a skeleton of cartilage instead of bone and are vertebrates all the same.
There are more species of fish than species of amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals put together.

teile.einleitung: Anaemia, sometimes called “poor blood”, is present when the blood contains too little of the red blood pigment or too few red blood cells. Then the blood cannot carry enough oxygen. The most common cause is a lack of iron.
wichtigste: Anaemia means a lack of healthy blood.
In anaemia, the blood is short of the red blood pigment, haemoglobin.
If red blood cells get too little iron, anaemia can develop.
Typical signs are tiredness, paleness and shortness of breath.
Iron is found, for example, in meat, pulses and wholegrain products.
A blood test shows whether someone has anaemia.
The treatment depends on the cause.

abschnitte.text: The word **anaemia** comes from Greek and means “without blood”. But it does not mean that blood is missing: it means that the blood contains too little **haemoglobin**. Haemoglobin is the red pigment in the red blood cells. It binds oxygen in the lungs and carries it to all the organs.

To make haemoglobin, the body needs **iron**. If iron is missing, fewer and smaller red blood cells are made. A lack of iron can arise if you eat too little iron or lose a lot of blood. During growth and pregnancy, too, the need for iron is higher.

People with anaemia are often tired and quickly worn out. The skin and the inside of the eyelids look pale. When climbing stairs you get out of breath more quickly and the heart beats faster. Sometimes there are also headaches, dizziness or brittle nails.

Not every anaemia comes from a lack of iron. A lack of **vitamin B12** or folic acid can also cause anaemia. In some inherited diseases such as **sickle cell anaemia**, the red blood cells have the wrong shape. Diseases of the bone marrow, where blood is made, can also be a cause.

A balanced diet with meat, lentils, beans, oats and green vegetables provides iron. Vitamin C, for example from oranges or peppers, helps the body to take up iron from plants. If the lack is severe, the doctor prescribes iron tablets or a drip. It is always important to find out the cause.
